correctness.rationale: For every positive three-run composition, ordered embedding pairs are partitioned exhaustively by intersection sizes 2, 1, 0; their weights are respectively 4, 2, 1. The disjoint case has six labeled-hole shapes, counted U twice and V four times by exact source-index matching. Algebra gives the claimed order-sensitive correction. The run-multiset lemma, positivity of the lengths and fixed product abc then recover the center run, including singleton and repeated-length boundaries. The packaged checker compares independently generated embedding pairs/shapes in 216 exact cases and independently computed host subsequence counts in 81 cases, all passing. No finite experiment is used to infer an infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The original 2023 primary paper poses this exact strong-Wilf equivalence characterization as Conjecture 5.2 and proves only the unordered-run invariant, while the present three-run result adds the order-sensitive two-insertion moment identity. Tian (2025) supplies an algorithm for individual subsequence counts, Bruda (2026) supplies eventual-polynomial frequency counts for fixed k, and Janson--Szpankowski (2020) supplies asymptotic random-host statistics; none inspected states or implies the ordered-middle recovery. Targeted published-record and accessible historical-claim searches found no identical or dominating result. Priority risk from an unindexed equivalence remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed result, unpublished manuscript, or general formula with previously unnoticed corollary might establish the same three-run classification.
The theorem is a proper subclass of the unrestricted Conjecture 5.2; nothing here proves its higher-run cases.

value.rationale: This proves the 2023 Menon--Singh strong Wilf equivalence conjecture for the natural infinite subfamily with at most three constant-letter runs, a structural question left open in that original paper. Only occurrence-frequency information at two near-minimal host lengths is required, rather than the entire infinite distribution. The order-sensitive singleton-middle correction identifies why the previously known run-multiset invariant was insufficient. This is a motivated classification with clear utility for pattern identifiability and not a routine parameter substitution.
